title: The Curious Tradition of Words of the Year (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds，在这档节目里，你可以听引人入胜的故事，了解这个世界奇妙又有趣的一面，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it’s the start of a new year, and also the start of a new three-part mini-series, all on the theme of “words and language”.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天是新一年的开始，也是一个全新三集迷你系列的开始，主题都是围绕“词汇与语言”。

sentences.en: In part one, today’s episode, we are going to talk about “Words Of The Year” - the words chosen each year by dictionaries for their particular cultural importance that year.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分，也就是今天这一集，我们要聊的是“年度词汇”——各大词典每年选出的、因当年特殊文化意义而入选的词汇。

sentences.en: In part two, we are going to talk about the concept of euphemisms in English - when you describe something unpleasant or uncomfortable in a more friendly way.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分，我们会聊聊英语中的委婉语这一概念——也就是用更友好的方式来描述令人不快或不舒服的事情。

sentences.en: And in part three, we are going to talk about the word “enshittification”.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分，我们会聊聊“enshittification”这个词。

sentences.en: It was coined in 2022, but we’ll look at what it means, how it has evolved since then, and what it tells us about the world we live in.
sentences.zh: 这个词是在 2022 年被创造出来的，我们会看看它的含义、之后是如何演变的，以及它对我们所生活的世界说明了什么。

sentences.en: Ok then, let’s get right into it and talk about words of the year.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们就直接进入正题，聊聊年度词汇。

sentences.en: One of the great, but also frustrating things, about language is that it is constantly evolving.
sentences.zh: 语言有一点既美妙又让人头疼，那就是它一直在不断演变。

sentences.en: Words change their meaning. Spellings change.
sentences.zh: 词义会变，拼写会变。

sentences.en: Grammar changes. Words stop being used. And entirely new words are introduced.
sentences.zh: 语法会变，有些词会被淘汰不用，还会有全新的词被创造出来。

sentences.en: And the more people that speak a language, and the greater the variety of people who speak that language, the more this is the case.
sentences.zh: 使用一门语言的人越多，使用这门语言的人群越多样化，这种变化就越明显。

sentences.en: English, with its hundreds of millions of native speakers and billions more non-native speakers, spread over practically every country in the world, is in a constant state of evolution.
sentences.zh: 英语拥有数亿母语使用者，还有数十亿非母语使用者，几乎遍布世界每一个国家，因此一直处于持续演变的状态之中。

sentences.en: One of the ways in which lexicographers try to document this evolution of language is by choosing a “word of the year”, a word or expression in English that has been of particular cultural significance that year.
sentences.zh: 词典编纂者记录这种语言演变的一种方式，就是评选“年度词汇”——即当年在文化上具有特殊意义的一个英语单词或表达。

sentences.en: It doesn’t have to be a completely new word, although often it is, but it has to be a word or expression that entered the language in a way it never had before.
sentences.zh: 它不一定非得是一个全新的词，虽然大多数时候确实是，但它必须是一个以前所未有的方式进入语言使用的词汇或表达。

sentences.en: Now, I should start by saying that defining a “Word of the Year” isn’t actually an English-language invention; it was “inspired” by the German tradition of Wort des Jahres, “Word of the Year” in German, which started in 1971.
sentences.zh: 首先要说明的是，“年度词汇”这个概念其实并非英语世界的发明，它是受德语传统 Wort des Jahres(德语中的“年度词汇”)“启发”而来，这一传统始于 1971 年。

sentences.en: It’s now a tradition followed by most major English-language dictionaries, including the Cambridge and Oxford Dictionaries, Merriam-Webster, Dictionary.com, as well as the American Dialect Society and the Australian National Dictionary Centre, which reflect language used in American and Australian English, respectively.
sentences.zh: 如今，这已经成为大多数主流英语词典都会遵循的传统，包括剑桥词典和牛津词典、韦氏词典、Dictionary.com，还有美国方言学会以及反映澳大利亚英语用法的澳大利亚国家词典中心。

sentences.en: So, what we are going to do today is talk about this tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们要聊的，就是这项传统。

sentences.en: We’ll start by talking about how it works and the process of how a word ends up being chosen as “Word of the Year”.
sentences.zh: 我们先来聊聊它是如何运作的，一个词最终是怎样被选为“年度词汇”的。

sentences.en: Then we’ll talk about some of the particularly interesting ones from the past 20 years or so, and we’ll end by talking about the words of the year for 2025.
sentences.zh: 接着，我们会聊聊过去二十年左右一些特别有意思的年度词汇，最后再聊聊 2025 年的年度词汇。

sentences.en: Let’s start with the basics. How do dictionaries actually choose a word of the year?
sentences.zh: 我们先从基础说起：词典到底是怎么选出年度词汇的？

sentences.en: Well, it all depends slightly on who you ask.
sentences.zh: 这个嘛，答案多少要看你问的是哪家词典。

sentences.en: But broadly speaking, it’s a combination of data and editorial judgement.
sentences.zh: 但总体来说，这是数据分析和编辑判断相结合的结果。

sentences.en: Most major dictionaries now analyse enormous databases of written and spoken English.
sentences.zh: 如今，大多数主流词典都会分析规模庞大的英语书面和口语数据库。

sentences.en: This used to be primarily from things like newspapers, books, the radio and TV, but it’s expanded to include everywhere that language is recorded: social media, YouTube videos, podcasts, and so on.
sentences.zh: 过去这些数据主要来自报纸、书籍、广播和电视，但如今已经扩展到了所有记录语言的地方：社交媒体、YouTube 视频、播客等等。

sentences.en: By analysing this data, lexicographers can identify which words are being used more than usual, which words have appeared out of nowhere, and which words have suddenly taken on new meanings.
sentences.zh: 通过分析这些数据，词典编纂者能够识别出哪些词的使用频率异常升高、哪些词是凭空冒出来的、哪些词又突然有了新的含义。

sentences.en: So that’s the data side. But it’s not just a question of numbers.
sentences.zh: 这是数据的一面。但这并不只是数字的问题。

sentences.en: It also involves people sitting down and thinking carefully about what a particular word tells us about that year.
sentences.zh: 这还需要人坐下来，仔细思考某个特定的词能说明这一年发生了什么。

sentences.en: Not just how often it was used, but why.
sentences.zh: 不只是这个词被用了多少次，更重要的是为什么会被这样使用。

sentences.en: What does it reveal about how people were feeling, what they were talking about, and what mattered most in that particular moment?
sentences.zh: 它揭示了人们当时的感受、人们在谈论什么、以及在那个特定时刻什么才是最重要的？

sentences.en: That’s the editorial side. And some dictionaries even add a third element.
sentences.zh: 这就是编辑判断的一面。而有些词典甚至还会加入第三个环节。

sentences.en: They release a shortlist, but put it to a public vote, letting members of the general population decide what the word of the year should be.
sentences.zh: 他们会公布一份候选名单，然后交由公众投票，让普罗大众来决定年度词汇该是哪一个。

sentences.en: And while each dictionary might have its own criteria, there are usually a few common themes.
sentences.zh: 尽管每家词典可能都有自己的评选标准，但通常都会出现一些共同的主题。

sentences.en: Words that reflect politics, culture, technology, social movements, and, more recently, the internet and how we talk online.
sentences.zh: 比如反映政治、文化、科技、社会运动的词汇，以及最近越来越常见的、和互联网以及我们线上交流方式相关的词汇。

sentences.en: So now that we’ve covered the basics of how the word of the year is chosen, let’s take a look at some actual examples.
sentences.zh: 好了，既然我们已经了解了年度词汇是如何评选出来的基本情况，那我们就来看几个实际的例子。

sentences.en: We won’t go through every year, but I want to share a few highlights from the past couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 我们不会逐年细数，但我想分享过去二十来年里的一些亮点。

sentences.en: Some are funny, some are serious, some are quite surprising, and others you might already use in your everyday English.
sentences.zh: 有些挺有趣，有些很严肃，有些相当令人意外，还有一些你可能在日常英语中已经在用了。

sentences.en: Let’s start by going back to 2005. That year, the American Dialect Society chose the word “truthiness”.
sentences.zh: 我们先回到 2005 年。那一年，美国方言学会选出的词是“truthiness”。

sentences.en: Now, although you might look at that word or hear that word and think, “I haven’t seen that before, but ok, it has 'truth' in it, and 'iness' probably means the quality of whatever the adjective or noun was, in this case 'truth’.
sentences.zh: 当你看到或听到这个词时，可能会想：“我以前没见过这个词，不过没关系，它里面有 'truth' 这个词根，而 'iness' 大概表示前面那个形容词或名词的某种性质，在这里就是 'truth'。

sentences.en: So maybe ‘truthiness’ means something like 'the quality of being true’”.
sentences.zh: 所以‘truthiness’大概意思可能是‘真实的性质’吧。”

sentences.en: That would be a perfectly good guess, perfectly reasonable, but it isn’t right.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完全合理、说得通的猜测，但其实并不正确。

sentences.en: “Truthiness” was a term popularised by the American comedian Stephen Colbert to mean something that feels like it should be true, even if it isn’t.
sentences.zh: “Truthiness”是由美国喜剧演员 Stephen Colbert 推广开来的一个词，意思是某件事让人感觉它应该是真的，即便实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: It was a new word for an old idea: the idea that people often believe what they want to be true, not what is actually true.
sentences.zh: 这是一个用来表达老观念的新词：人们往往相信自己希望是真的东西，而不是真正的事实。

sentences.en: With Colbert, he used it to criticise politicians and media figures who weren’t so interested in the facts, just in what sounded good and felt like it was true.
sentences.zh: Colbert 用这个词来批评那些对事实本身不太感兴趣、只在乎听起来顺耳、感觉像是真的的政客和媒体人物。

sentences.en: In particular, it was aimed at President George W.
sentences.zh: 这尤其针对的是乔治·W.

sentences.en: Bush and his famously strong convictions, like the existence of Saddam Hussein’s weapons of mass destruction, even if there wasn’t any evidence.
sentences.zh: 布什总统，以及他那些出了名的坚定信念，比如坚信萨达姆·侯赛因拥有大规模杀伤性武器，尽管根本没有任何证据。

sentences.en: A nice word, right? Jumping ahead to 2013, Oxford Dictionaries chose “selfie” as its word of the year.
sentences.zh: 是不是挺有意思的一个词？时间跳到 2013 年，牛津词典选出的年度词汇是“selfie”(自拍)。

sentences.en: As you no doubt know, a “selfie” is the word for a photo you take of yourself, typically with your phone.
sentences.zh: 你肯定知道，“selfie”指的是自己给自己拍的照片，通常是用手机拍的。

sentences.en: And although it probably seems completely unbelievable to anyone under the age of 18, anyone who lived before the iPhone and Instagram will know that this wasn’t something that people always did, so there wasn’t really a need for a word to describe it.
sentences.zh: 对 18 岁以下的人来说，这大概难以置信，但经历过 iPhone 和 Instagram 出现之前那个年代的人都知道，过去人们并不总是这么做，所以也就没有太大必要专门用一个词来描述它。

sentences.en: It’s interesting to mention this because the inclusion of this word as “word of the year” clearly pinpoints this cultural shift.
sentences.zh: 提到这一点挺有意思的，因为这个词被选为“年度词汇”，清楚地标记出了这种文化转变发生的节点。

sentences.en: And if a historian in 100 years needs to figure out the exact date when humans started taking pictures of themselves en masse, well, the choice of ‘selfie’ as Word Of The Year provides a pretty good clue.
sentences.zh: 如果一百年后的历史学家想弄清楚人类究竟是从什么时候开始大规模自拍的，那么‘selfie’被选为年度词汇，就提供了一个相当不错的线索。

sentences.en: And we can go on. In 2016, ‘post-truth’ was the word of the year.
sentences.zh: 我们继续往下看。2016 年的年度词汇是‘post-truth’(后真相)。

sentences.en: This referred to a time when objective facts seemed to matter less than emotions or personal beliefs.
sentences.zh: 这个词指的是这样一个时代：客观事实似乎变得不如情绪或个人信念重要。

sentences.en: It was the year of Brexit, the US presidential election, and intense political polarisation.
sentences.zh: 那一年发生了英国脱欧公投、美国总统大选，政治两极分化也异常激烈。

sentences.en: It’s a pretty depressing word, but one that definitely captured the feeling of the time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当令人沮丧的词，但它确实精准地捕捉到了那个时代的情绪。

sentences.en: In 2022, Oxford let the public vote on the word of the year, and the winner was “goblin mode”.
sentences.zh: 2022 年，牛津词典把年度词汇的决定权交给公众投票，最终胜出的是“goblin mode”(哥布林模式)。

sentences.en: A goblin, if you don’t know this word, is a sort of imaginary, naughty, often ugly creature that plays tricks on humans.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道 goblin 这个词是什么意思，它指的是一种虚构的、调皮捣蛋、通常长得丑陋、喜欢捉弄人类的生物。

sentences.en: And “goblin mode” describes a kind of lazy, messy, and unapologetically unbothered attitude.
sentences.zh: 而“goblin mode”描述的是一种懒散、邋遢、毫不在意别人看法、理直气壮不上进的态度。

sentences.en: Someone in goblin mode might be eating junk food in bed and ignoring all responsibilities, simply not caring about what anyone else thinks.
sentences.zh: 处于“goblin mode”的人，可能会窝在床上吃垃圾食品，对一切责任都不闻不问，完全不在乎别人怎么想。

sentences.en: It’s not a polite word necessarily, but it clearly resonated with a lot of people who were feeling burnt out or just done with pretending to be productive all the time.
sentences.zh: 这算不上是一个多么“文雅”的词，但它显然引起了很多人的共鸣——那些感到身心俱疲、不想再假装自己一直很高效的人。

sentences.en: And that brings us to the present. In a moment, we'll look at the words that were chosen in 2025, but before we do, I want to just have a quick pause to ask what all these words have in common.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就聊到了现在。稍后我们会看看 2025 年选出的年度词汇，不过在那之前，我想先停一下，问一个问题：这些词有什么共同点？

sentences.en: They aren’t just words really. They are signs.
sentences.zh: 它们其实不只是单词，更是一种信号。

sentences.en: They reflect what people are thinking about, what people are worried about, what they’re joking about, and how language adapts to express new ideas or feelings.
sentences.zh: 它们反映出人们在想什么、担心什么、拿什么开玩笑，以及语言是如何调整自身来表达新的想法或感受的。

sentences.en: So with that in mind, let’s turn our attention to 2025.
sentences.zh: 带着这个想法，我们把目光转向 2025 年。

sentences.en: What were the words of the year this time?
sentences.zh: 这一次的年度词汇是什么呢？

sentences.en: And what do they tell us about the moment we are living in?
sentences.zh: 它们又能告诉我们，我们正身处一个怎样的时代？

sentences.en: One of them is a bit surprising. It’s not even a real word in the traditional sense.
sentences.zh: 其中一个词有点出人意料，严格来说它甚至算不上一个传统意义上的“词”。

sentences.en: It’s 6 7. Yes, the numbers six seven. That was chosen by Dictionary.com as its word of the year for 2025.
sentences.zh: 它是“6 7”。没错，就是数字六和七。这是 Dictionary.com 选出的 2025 年年度词汇。

sentences.en: If you’ve heard of this word before, it’s probably because you have young kids, and if you haven’t heard of it before and you’re wondering what it means, the honest answer is… nobody really seems to know.
sentences.zh: 如果你之前听说过这个词，那很可能是因为你家里有小孩；如果你从没听过，正好奇它是什么意思，老实说……好像谁也说不清楚。

sentences.en: I have a six-year-old son, and one of his friends came over to play the other day.
sentences.zh: 我有个六岁的儿子，前几天他的一个朋友来家里玩。

sentences.en: I asked him–in Swedish, because we live in Sweden–how are you, and he responded “six seven”, the English expression “six seven”.
sentences.zh: 我用瑞典语问他(因为我们住在瑞典)最近怎么样，他回答的却是“six seven”，就是英语里的“six seven”这个说法。

sentences.en: His mum shrugged and said she didn’t really know why he said this, and it seems like there is no definite answer to what it means.
sentences.zh: 他妈妈耸耸肩，说她也不太清楚他为什么会这么说，看起来这个词到底是什么意思，确实没有一个明确的答案。

sentences.en: According to Dictionary.com, 6 7 became popular on TikTok and other social media platforms in 2024 and 2025.
sentences.zh: 根据 Dictionary.com 的说法，“6 7”是在 2024 年和 2025 年间，在 TikTok 等社交媒体平台上流行起来的。

sentences.en: It started off as an in-joke, then a trend, then a meme, and somehow ended up becoming a phrase that means everything and nothing at the same time.
sentences.zh: 它最初只是一个圈内梗，后来变成一种潮流，再后来变成一个梗图素材，最后不知怎么就变成了一个既什么都能表示、又什么都不表示的短语。

sentences.en: Young people have used it in videos, comments, as a gesture, as a sort of catch-all response to almost anything.
sentences.zh: 年轻人会在视频里、评论区里用它，也会用一个手势来表示它，把它当作几乎可以回应任何事情的万能答案。

sentences.en: If someone asks a question and you don’t really want to answer, you can just say “six seven”.
sentences.zh: 如果有人问了个问题，而你并不想回答，你就可以直接说“six seven”。

sentences.en: If you’re joking around with a friend and want to tease them, just say “six seven”.
sentences.zh: 如果你在和朋友开玩笑、想调侃对方，也可以直接说“six seven”。

sentences.en: It means whatever you want it to mean, and that’s kind of the point.
sentences.zh: 它可以是你想让它表示的任何意思，而这大概正是它的意义所在。

sentences.en: The team at Dictionary.com described it as “a playful, Gen Alpha expression of absurdist internet humour”.
sentences.zh: Dictionary.com 的团队将它描述为“一种俏皮的、阿尔法世代式的、带有荒诞色彩的网络幽默表达”。

sentences.en: It’s chaotic, slightly annoying, kind of meaningless, and oddly fascinating.
sentences.zh: 它混乱、略带烦人、有点没什么意义，却又莫名地让人着迷。

sentences.en: And importantly, if you are old enough to vote, you’re probably too old to use it.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，如果你已经到了可以投票的年纪，那你大概也已经“太老”了，用不了这个词了。

sentences.en: So “6 7” was one of the words that was chosen.
sentences.zh: 所以“6 7”就是入选的年度词汇之一。

sentences.en: The Collins Dictionary, interestingly enough, didn’t even include it in its shortlist.
sentences.zh: 有意思的是，柯林斯词典甚至都没把它列入候选名单。

sentences.en: There were 10 words shortlisted for its potential word of the year: ‘aura farming’, ‘biohacking’, ‘broligarchy’, ‘clanker’, ‘coolcation’, ‘glaze’, ‘HENRY’, ‘microretirement’, ‘taskmasking’, and ‘vibe coding’.
sentences.zh: 柯林斯词典的年度词汇候选名单一共有 10 个词：‘aura farming’、‘biohacking’、‘broligarchy’、‘clanker’、‘coolcation’、‘glaze’、‘HENRY’、‘microretirement’、‘taskmasking’，以及‘vibe coding’。

sentences.en: We can actually go through them one by one, quickly.
sentences.zh: 我们其实可以快速地把它们一一过一遍。

sentences.en: Aura farming is when people post highly edited or curated photos online to boost their image.
sentences.zh: Aura farming 指的是人们在网上发布经过精心修饰、刻意打造的照片，以此来提升自己的形象。

sentences.en: Biohacking is the idea of using science or self-experimentation to try to improve your body or mind.
sentences.zh: Biohacking 指的是利用科学手段或自我实验，来尝试改善自己身体或大脑状态的做法。

sentences.en: Broligarchy describes a group of powerful men who are all close friends, a kind of brotherly oligarchy.
sentences.zh: Broligarchy 描述的是一群彼此关系亲密的权势男性，是一种“兄弟式寡头统治”。

sentences.en: Clanker is a derogatory term used for a computer.
sentences.zh: Clanker 是用来指代电脑的一个贬义词。

sentences.en: Coolcation is a holiday somewhere cool. Not cool as in fashionable, but cool in temperature, often taken to escape extreme heat.
sentences.zh: Coolcation 指的是去凉爽地方度假，这里的“cool”不是指时髦，而是指气温低，通常是为了躲避酷暑。

sentences.en: Glaze is to excessively or undeservedly praise someone.
sentences.zh: Glaze 指的是过度地、名不副实地吹捧某人。

sentences.en: HENRY, all in capital letters, stands for “high earner, not rich yet”, which is used to describe someone who earns a lot of money but still feels financially squeezed.
sentences.zh: HENRY 全部大写，是“high earner, not rich yet”(高收入但还没富起来)的缩写，用来形容那些收入很高、但依然感觉手头紧的人。

sentences.en: Microretirement means taking a break from work, not forever, but for a while, like a mini retirement earlier in life.
sentences.zh: Microretirement 指的是暂时从工作中抽身休息一段时间，不是永久退休，更像是人生早期的一次“迷你退休”。

sentences.en: Taskmasking is pretending to multitask, when in reality you’re just switching between tasks and not doing any of them well.
sentences.zh: Taskmasking 指的是假装自己在同时处理多项任务，但实际上只是在各项任务之间来回切换，却没有一件做得好。

sentences.en: And finally, vibe coding, which is using AI tools to build software, and it was this that was the winner.
sentences.zh: 最后是 vibe coding，指的是用 AI 工具来开发软件，而最终胜出、成为年度词汇的正是这一个。

sentences.en: Vibe coding, if you haven’t heard the expression, refers to the way that people are now using artificial intelligence to write computer code.
sentences.zh: 如果你没听过 vibe coding 这个说法，它指的是人们现在借助人工智能来编写计算机代码的这样一种方式。

sentences.en: Instead of sitting down and typing out hundreds of lines of code manually, people–like me–are now “prompting” AI tools with natural language.
sentences.zh: 人们——比如我自己——现在不再是坐下来手动敲出成百上千行代码，而是用自然语言向 AI 工具“提要求”。

sentences.en: Last year, I built a Chrome Extension that helps people learn new English vocabulary, as well as a tool that gives you feedback on your written English, and both of those were “vibe-coded”.
sentences.zh: 去年，我做了一个帮助大家学习新英语词汇的 Chrome 扩展，还做了一个能对你的英语写作给出反馈的工具，这两个都是“vibe-coded”出来的。

sentences.en: I have some knowledge of software development, but most of the code was written by AI, with me checking it, rather than it being written from scratch by me.
sentences.zh: 我对软件开发略懂一些，但大部分代码都是 AI 写的，我负责检查，而不是从零开始自己写。

sentences.en: If you've done this yourself, you’ll know it's pretty magical.
sentences.zh: 如果你自己也这样做过，你就会知道这个过程相当神奇。

sentences.en: It’s a completely new way of building software, and it’s changing who gets to call themselves a “coder”.
sentences.zh: 这是一种全新的软件开发方式，也正在改变谁有资格自称是“程序员”。

sentences.en: You no longer need to know every programming language.
sentences.zh: 你不再需要精通每一门编程语言。

sentences.en: If you know how to ask the AI in the right way, in some cases that can be enough.
sentences.zh: 只要你懂得用正确的方式向 AI 提问，在某些情况下，这样就足够了。

sentences.en: So that’s vibe coding. And like 6 7, it says something about the time we are living in.
sentences.zh: 这就是 vibe coding。和“6 7”一样，它也在诉说着我们所处的这个时代。

sentences.en: One word reflects how fast the next generation is playing with language and identity online.
sentences.zh: 一个词反映出下一代人在网络上摆弄语言和身份认同的速度有多快。

sentences.en: The other reflects how fast our relationship with technology is changing, especially when it comes to work, creativity, and skills.
sentences.zh: 另一个词则反映出我们与科技之间的关系正在多快地发生变化，尤其是在工作、创造力和技能这些方面。

sentences.en: But will people still talk about ‘vibe coding’ in 20 years?
sentences.zh: 但二十年后，人们还会不会继续讨论‘vibe coding’呢？

sentences.en: Well, most probably not. Software development might not exist in exactly the same way, and the probability of someone typing “create a signup form” into a text interface seems…slim.
sentences.zh: 很可能不会了。软件开发到时候的形态，大概率已经和现在不完全一样，到那时还有人在文本界面里敲“帮我做一个注册表单”这种指令的概率……似乎不高。

sentences.en: And as for ‘6 7’, well, like anything that starts as an ‘in-joke’, as soon as it enters the mainstream, it ceases to be funny, and stops being used, so the probability of anyone knowing what ‘6 7’ means in even 10 years time seems equally slim.
sentences.zh: 至于‘6 7’嘛，就跟任何起源于“圈内梗”的东西一样，一旦进入主流，就不再有趣了，也就不再有人用了，所以哪怕只是十年后，还有人知道‘6 7’是什么意思的概率，似乎同样不高。

sentences.en: Some words of the year, however, do have staying power.
sentences.zh: 不过，也有一些年度词汇确实经受住了时间的考验。

sentences.en: In 2005, the New Oxford American Dictionary declared its word of the year to be a word meaning "a digital recording of a radio broadcast or similar program, made available on the internet for downloading to a personal audio player”, a word that derived from a mixture of “broadcast” and “iPod”.
sentences.zh: 2005 年，《新牛津美语词典》选出的年度词汇，意思是“将广播节目或类似内容进行数字录制，并放到网上供人下载到个人音频播放器中收听”，这个词是由“broadcast”(广播)和“iPod”组合而来的。

sentences.en: The word was, as you might have guessed, podcast.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经猜到了，这个词就是 podcast(播客)。

sentences.en: Back then, 20 years ago, it was not just a new word, but a new concept; the idea of downloading or streaming spoken content on demand was still relatively new.
sentences.zh: 那是二十年前，它不只是一个新词，更是一个全新的概念；按需下载或在线收听语音内容，在当时还是相对新鲜的事物。

sentences.en: Today, of course, podcasts are everywhere, including what you are listening to right now.
sentences.zh: 而今天，播客当然已经无处不在，包括你现在正在收听的这个节目也是。

sentences.en: So, on one level, these “words of the year” lists are a bit of harmless fun.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种层面上说，这些“年度词汇”榜单，不过是些无伤大雅的乐子。

sentences.en: A way for a dictionary to guarantee it’s going to make the news, and cultural commentators to have something to write about during a traditional slow period of the year, even if that word or expression is forgotten a matter of 12 months later.
sentences.zh: 对词典来说，这是一种能保证自己登上新闻的方式；对文化评论员来说，这是在一年中传统的新闻淡季里，能有个话题可写的机会，即便那个词或说法在十二个月后就会被人遗忘。

sentences.en: But on another level, they’re not just words.
sentences.zh: 但从另一个层面来看，它们又不只是单词而已。

sentences.en: They are snapshots. Tiny time capsules. A reflection of what people were talking about.
sentences.zh: 它们是快照，是一个个微型时间胶囊，映照出人们当时在谈论什么。

sentences.en: What people were paying attention to. What people were concerned about, confused by, or inventing.
sentences.zh: 人们当时在关注什么，在担忧什么，对什么感到困惑，又在创造着什么。

sentences.en: Some, of course, will fade away into obscurity.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些词最终会悄然淡出、被人遗忘。

sentences.en: Others might just shape the way we live and speak for many years to come.
sentences.zh: 而另一些，可能会在未来很多年里，持续塑造我们的生活方式和语言表达。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on Words Of The Year.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天这期关于年度词汇的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这一期你听得开心，也学到了一些新东西。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this was part one of a three-part mini-series on the theme of words and language.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是围绕“词汇与语言”主题的三集迷你系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up, we’ll be talking about euphemisms, and we’ll go through a bunch of commonly used ones in English.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们会聊聊委婉语，也会一起过一遍英语中一些常用的委婉说法。

sentences.en: And in part three, we’ll talk about the fantastic linguistic and cultural concept of enshittification.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分，我们会聊聊“enshittification”这个精彩的语言与文化概念。

sentences.en: You can find out more about that over at leonardoenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 你可以前往 leonardoenglish.com 了解更多相关内容。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 以上就是 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你平安，我们下一集再见。
